newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Portugal envoy heads U.N. Iraq sanctions committee.
newsitem.headline: Portugal envoy heads U.N. Iraq sanctions committee.

text.p: Portugal's new U.N. envoy, ambassador Antonio Monteiro, was elected on Monday as chairman of the Security Council's Iraqi sanctions committee.
The committee monitors sanctions in force against Iraq since its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait and approves the import by Baghdad of food, medicine and other exceptions to the sanctions regime.

The committee also plays a role in implementation of an "oil-for-food" plan which went into force last month and allows Iraq to export $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy humanitarian supplies to help offset the effects of sanctions on Iraqi civilians.

The Iraqi sanctions committee, like similar committees which monitor various types of sanctions relating to Libya, Somalia, Angola, Rwanda and Liberia, has the same 15-nation membership as the Security Council.
The membership of the council changed on Jan. 1 when Costa Rica, Japan, Kenya, Portugal and Sweden began two-year terms, replacing Botswana, Germany, Honduras, Indonesia and Italy.
Monteiro, 52, who has just arrived in New York to head Portugal's U.N. mission, takes over from ambassador Tono Eitel of Germany as chairman of the Iraqi sanctions body.
The two vice-chairmenships of the committee, allocated to member states rather than specific diplomats, went to Poland and Guinea-Bissau.
